A1.justification: Both complete 11-page PDFs describe the same EmotiCrafter work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and references support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-generation experiments, quantitative baseline comparisons, two user studies with 20 college students, and ablations in Section 4.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments, user-study outcomes, and ablation results in Section 4 and Tables 1–4.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same V-A encoders, modified GPT-2 emotion-injection transformer, SDXL conditioning, scaled residual learning, and density-weighted loss. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both use OASIS, EMOTIC, and FindingEmo to construct training prompts. The text-conditioned, empty-prompt, discrete-emotion, and continuous V-A generation scenarios remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Figure 6 and Table 1 retain Cross Attention, Time Embedding, Textual Inversion, and GPT-4+SDXL. GPT-4+SDXL also remains the comparator for continuity and user studies.

E3.justification: Both retain the same metrics and 3,300-image evaluation per method: 132 prompts with five valence and five arousal values. Training settings and both user-study designs, including participant and image-set counts, are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 retains the same scaling-factor sweep and density-weighting ablation in Figures 9–10 and Table 4. The qualitative analyses in Figures 5–7 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Tables 1–4 retain the same ± reporting. Section 4.3 retains the Shapiro-Wilk and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and Figure 8 retains its significance annotations. No run-count or seed information is added.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 and the figure results match. For example, Table 1 retains the proposed method's A/V errors of 1.828/1.510, and Table 2 retains LPIPS-Continuous values of 0.220 versus 0.361 for GPT-4+SDXL.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 retain the same mathematical content, including emotion injection, residual scaling, and KDE density weighting. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same C-EICG task proposal, claimed first dedicated model, emotion-embedding network, loss-function contribution, dataset contribution, and effectiveness claims.

C2.justification: Both retain the emotional-control versus semantic-fidelity interpretation and the same limitations: harder arousal control, excessive human-activity generation, and semantic shifts. Their proposed explanations and remedies are unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 retains the same prompt construction and verification details, two A800 GPUs, AdamW hyperparameters, 200 epochs, batch size 768, and 7–8-hour training time. The code link and code/data release statement are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 61 references and related-work positioning are retained. The changed citation back-reference page for GPT-2 reflects text reflow, not a change in the cited work or its role.

P1.justification: The affiliation and author footnote change 'Shanghai Innovation Institution' to 'Shanghai Innovation Institute.' Minor paragraph and spacing edits occur, while the substantive prose and section organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 4 moves from the right column to beneath Figure 10 in the left column of page 8. Text, equations, and references reflow, bringing the full limitations discussion onto page 8. Figure content and table structure are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 adjusts affiliation wording and presentation while preserving the method, evidence, claims, reproducibility information, and limitations. The limited reflow and Table 4 relocation produce no meaningful overall difference in clarity or scientific support.
